correctness.rationale: For every digit transition, the specified paired count matrix is explicit. The standalone exact 16x16 characteristic polynomial verifies the six simple modulus-two eigenvalues, a simple 4-eigenvalue whose uniform eigenvector is orthogonal to the signed observable, one simple eigenvalue 1 and nilpotent zero part. The radix-block bound is uniform in all starting states, implying the O(sqrt N) estimate for all integers N. Nonconstant values at k=8 and k=9 force a nonzero modulus-two coefficient, and distinct unimodular phases have positive Cesaro mean square, proving sharpness. Direct nested-recurrence checks to 262144 indices, direct 4-power sums and partial radix-block checks corroborate, but do not replace, the proof.

The published individual DFAOs provide inputs, not the sixteen-state joint spectrum or its sharp consequence. An exact calculation with a characteristic polynomial and nonzero modulus-two modes gives a non-routine sharp quantitative relation between these particular sequences.

value.rationale: This is a motivated comparison of two newly introduced individually balanced nested-origin automatic sequences. Sharp square-root cancellation gives a quantitative independence law at the same positions, for all prefixes, and proves optimal fluctuations via a nonzero spectrum. Such a law is neither a restatement of their separate balance nor implied by generic automaticity. The structural joint spectrum answers a meaningful question opened by their separate automata and factor-complexity comparison.
